definition_complete: decoder: accept + size reject + spec alignment (accept_spec_k, reject_size_spec, reject_complete) + Desc codec equality / correspondence + accept witness + reject witness, all kernel-checked theorems with standard axioms; accept / reject / spec_k / reject_size_spec theorems keyed to the function by the code constant in their type (the function is the subject: no other target code constant of the theorem calls it); witnesses and spec theorems use the mapped accept / reject theorem
complete_does_not_include: `runtime.writeBarrier` != 0 (every accept theorem assumes the flag word is 0)
runtime callee bodies (makeslice / memmove / growslice / newobject / fmt.errorf: contract hypotheses, MakesliceC / MemmoveC / ...)
callee error returns (the `fmt.Errorf` wrap paths of delegated fields; `reject_complete` covers the size path condition only)
growslice / T-7 (encoder capacity growth beyond the listed theorems)
x86-64 hardware execution (semantics = Kraken's model of the amd64 instructions; no hardware run)
cannot_detect: a row whose `codec` or `reject_complete` names ANOTHER type's theorem: these two parts are checked for existence, kind and axioms only (their types hold no code constant, their proofs use no mapped theorem; review g5c-r1 m03, m04). Keying them to the row's Desc constant needs a new column in `inventory_decls.lean`; not done
that a theorem's statement says what its part name means (accept, reject, spec): the mapping table is hand-written; the statements are checked by review and by the kinds, not by this script
a theorem with two target code constants of which neither calls the other (it fails: no single subject)
that <decls.tsv> was made on the built tree of the same commit (its header has the Lean version, no commit id)

that an encoder row's premise text and NOT-proved text say what the mapped reject / growslice theorems assume (hand-written per row, unit E2-C2; checked by review against the theorem statements, not by this script)
methods outside `github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/v7/` (e.g. `github.com/holiman/uint256`) and SSZ methods with names outside the listed kinds
